learningObjective: At index i, combine the product strictly before i with the product strictly after i.

mechanismReview.pattern: Prefix and suffix accumulation without division.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: Each output excludes exactly one array position, division is forbidden, and multiplication can be accumulated from either boundary.
mechanismReview.invariant: Before prefix index i, prefix is the product of nums[0..i-1]. Before suffix index i, suffix is the product of nums[i+1..n-1], while out[i] already stores the left product.
mechanismReview.stateModel: The output array stores completed left products; one scalar prefix scans right, then one scalar suffix scans left. No separate prefix or suffix arrays are required.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: An indexed array whose cells pair each input with its current output makes both passes and every multiplication readable in static HTML; the stable scan key visibly reverses direction between passes.
rejectedAlternatives: A final prefix/suffix table hides the order in which the implementation writes and multiplies each cell.
A division formula does not represent the supplied algorithm and breaks on zeros.
A prose-only trace forces the reader to remember four changing output values.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: When every answer excludes one position and the operation is associative, save the contribution from one side and sweep the other side with a scalar; the same decomposition works for left/right minima, maxima, and cumulative constraints.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.
